items.question: Which virtues and which sixteenfold group are located in the person principle down to earth?
premises: Service, purity, contentment, and straightness complete the ten declared qualities.
These qualities belong in the person principle.
A sixteenfold group is situated there extending down to earth.
items.inference: The person principle contains the completed set of ten virtues and a sixteenfold group reaching to the earth level.
uncertainties: The exact members of the sixteenfold group are not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: Service, purity, contentment, and straightness complete the ten declared qualities in the person principle. Again, a sixteenfold group is situated there, extending down to earth.

items.question: What groups arise from the world called the body-bond upward through intellect and ego?
premises: Starting from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect come next.
In that same place there are eight forms of ego in three ways.
Desire and other related factors are also present there.
items.inference: The cosmological sequence from the body-bond world includes intellect qualities, an eightfold threefold ego, and desire-related factors.
uncertainties: The precise identity of the desire-and-others group is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Beginning from the world called the body-bond, there come the qualities of intellect. There too are the eightfold ego in three forms, and likewise desire and the rest.

items.question: How are the bonds in the person classified and what effect do they have on liberation?
premises: The bonds are divided into adventitious, lords-of-groups, and lords-of-knowledge types.
These three kinds are situated in the person.
They obstruct the path of liberation.
items.inference: Three classes of bonds located in the person block progress toward liberation.
uncertainties: The verse does not explain how each class obstructs in a distinct way.
items.plain_english: The bonds, divided into adventitious, lords of groups, and lords of knowledge, are threefold. Situated in the person, they obstruct the path of liberation.

items.question: What is defined as a bond in relation to supreme nondual Shiva?
premises: Supreme Shiva is described as nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty.
Anything other than that supreme Shiva is being defined.
Such otherness is called a bond.
items.inference: A bond is anything that falls short of or differs from the supreme nondual consciousness-freedom of Shiva.
items.plain_english: Whatever is other than the supreme, beautiful freedom of nondual consciousness, other than the supreme Shiva as described, is called a bond.

items.question: Why do persons arise when the supreme Lord is already full even in personhood?
premises: The supreme Lord remains full even when personhood is attained.
In that state there is non-recognition of his own nature.
This non-recognition is described as wondrous and gives rise to persons.
items.inference: Personhood arises through non-recognition of the Lord's own full nature, not through any lack in the Lord.
items.plain_english: Thus, even when the supreme Lord, though full, has attained personhood, there is non-recognition of his own nature. This is wondrous indeed, and from it persons arise.

items.question: How does a person become liberated from all bonds present in personhood?
premises: All bonds, whether stated or unstated, are characterized as taught in another scripture.
All these bonds are present in the person.
By purifying those bonds there, one is liberated from becoming.
items.inference: Liberation from worldly becoming comes through purifying all bonds present in the person.
uncertainties: The method of purification is not described in this verse.
items.plain_english: All the bonds, whether stated or unstated, as characterized in other teachings, are present in the person. By purifying them there, one is liberated from worldly becoming.

items.question: Which divine inhabitants are found above the person in necessity and in time?
premises: Above the person, in the principle of necessity, there are ten golden-lustrous Shankaras.
In the principle of time there are ten very white Shivas.
The verse distinguishes the two levels by location and appearance.
items.inference: The levels above the person are populated by ten Shankaras in necessity and ten Shivas in time, each with a distinct appearance.
items.plain_english: Above the person, in the principle of necessity, there are ten golden-lustrous Shankaras. In the principle of time, there are ten very white Shivas.

rows.grounds: location in the principle of attachment

items.question: What world and retinue are found in the principle of attachment?
premises: In the principle of attachment there is a world of the lord of heroes.
That world is a city of teachers and students.
Each has a retinue numbering ten million and sixteen thousand.
items.inference: The attachment principle contains the world of the lord of heroes, inhabited by teachers and students with vast retinues.
uncertainties: It is slightly ambiguous whether the count applies to each teacher-student pair or to each principal figure.
items.plain_english: In the principle of attachment is the world of the lord of heroes, a city of teachers and students. Each has a retinue of ten million and sixteen thousand.

items.question: What city and powers are present in the principle of impure knowledge?
premises: In impure knowledge there is a city brilliant with nine powers.
These powers extend up to Manonmani.
They are declared to begin with Vama.
items.inference: The impure knowledge principle contains a city illuminated by the nine powers from Vama to Manonmani.
items.plain_english: In impure knowledge there is a city shining with nine powers, extending up to Manonmani; these are declared to begin with Vama.

rows.grounds: location in the principle of kala

items.question: What worlds are found in kala and in the threefold maya above it?
premises: In kala there is the supreme city of the triad of great gods.
Above that is maya, described as threefold.
Maya is chiefly occupied by countless millions of Anantas.
items.inference: The cosmology moves from the triad's supreme city in kala to a threefold maya filled chiefly by innumerable Anantas.
uncertainties: The exact sense of tripuṭikā as threefold may refer to divisions not fully specified here.
items.plain_english: In kala is the supreme city of the triad of great gods. Above that is maya, threefold, chiefly occupied by countless millions of Anantas.

items.question: How is maya described in the Shaiva scripture and what group of great gods is mentioned there?
premises: Maya is pervaded by the cavities of bhaga.
This is taught in the Shaiva scripture.
The scripture also mentions a group of eight great gods extending to the measure of a thumb in the night.
items.inference: The Shaiva teaching presents maya as internally divided by bhaga-cavities and associates it with an eightfold group of great gods.
uncertainties: The phrase aṅguṣṭhamātraparyantaṃ niśi is obscure in this excerpt and may refer to a specific doctrinal division.
items.plain_english: That maya is pervaded by the cavities of bhaga, as taught in the Shaiva scripture. Again, it speaks of a group of eight great gods, extending to the measure of a thumb, in the night.

items.question: How do the Malini and Purva scriptures relate the Vama powers to different levels?
premises: The Malini teaching speaks of lordship over the eight circles.
The powers beginning with Vama were taught in the Purva scripture as beginning with the person.
The verse places these teachings in parallel.
items.inference: The same Vama powers are located differently across scriptural teachings, with Malini emphasizing eight-circle lordship and Purva placing them from the person upward.
uncertainties: The verse is compressed and does not fully spell out the mapping between the two scriptural accounts.
items.plain_english: Likewise, in the teaching of Shri Malini, there is lordship over the eight circles. The powers beginning with Vama, which were taught in the Shri Purva scripture as beginning with the person, are referred to here.

items.question: Where are these beings placed in the Shaiva scripture and what ascetic groups are associated with that level?
premises: Those beings are taught in the Shaiva scripture as located in the maya principle.
The account proceeds from Ananta onward.
Skull-vow observers, self-body sacrificers, and harsh ascetics are associated with that domain.
items.inference: The maya level, described from Ananta onward, includes severe ascetic practitioners among its inhabitants.
items.plain_english: In the Shaiva scripture they are taught as being in the maya principle, from Ananta onward. There are skull-vow observers, those who perform offerings in their own bodies, and practitioners of harsh austerity.

items.question: How do these ascetics progress through the principles and where do they arrive?
premises: They are fearless toward all and observe the sword-edge vow.
They know each principle.
They gradually go to each principle until they reach where the lord is called Ananta.
items.inference: Through severe discipline and knowledge of the principles, these ascetics ascend step by step to the domain of Ananta.
items.plain_english: Fearless toward all, observing the sword-edge vow, and knowing each principle, they gradually reach each principle in turn, until they come to where the lord is called Ananta.

items.question: What is said about the abode and role of the lord associated with Ananta?
premises: A place beyond is described as belonging to the lord of Ananta.
That deity performs maintenance, dissolution, and creation.
He is also the guardian of the door of the cave and bhaga.
items.inference: The cited teaching presents Ananta's lord as a cosmic ruler who governs the three acts and guards the threshold of the cave and bhaga.
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed and reads like a citation fragment.
items.plain_english: And it has been said: beyond is the abode of the lord of Ananta, the god who performs maintenance, dissolution, and creation, and who guards the door of the cave and of bhaga.

items.question: What does the lord draw out from the cavity of maya and give to persons?
premises: From the cavity of maya he draws things out repeatedly.
He gives virtues, powers such as smallness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogas.
These gifts are given to persons.
items.inference: The lord distributes a wide range of spiritual attainments and experiences to persons by drawing them out from the cavity of maya.
items.plain_english: Drawing them out again and again from the cavity of maya, he gives to persons virtues, powers beginning with smallness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogas.

items.question: How do Ananta and the other lords shine in their office within the cave?
premises: Their own strength is kindled by his power.
They function as lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.
All of them, from Ananta to those headed by Shatabhava, shine.
items.inference: Empowered by the higher lord, the whole series of cave-lords from Ananta to Shatabhava illuminate their domain.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the group headed by Shatabhava is not explained here.
items.plain_english: Strengthened by his power, all those headed by Ananta, down to those headed by Shatabhava, shine as lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.

items.question: Why does Shiva preside over the unmanifest and bring forth the world?
premises: Shiva presides over the unmanifest.
He brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu.
He is the cause of authority over the pure and impure streams.
items.inference: Shiva's cosmic activity over the unmanifest is authorized by Shambhu and establishes governance over both pure and impure streams.
items.plain_english: Presiding over the unmanifest, Shiva brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu, because he is the cause of authority over the pure and impure streams.

items.question: What role do beings established in that great Shiva-state first assume in the world?
premises: Some beings are established in that great state through connection with Shiva's qualities.
They are established there first.
They become makers of creation, maintenance, and dissolution for the world beginning with Ananta.
items.inference: Attainment of the great Shiva-state confers the primary cosmic functions over the world beginning with Ananta.
items.plain_english: Those who are first established in that great state through connection with the qualities of Shiva become the makers of creation, maintenance, and dissolution for the world beginning with Ananta.

items.question: What lies beyond the cavity of maya and how does it function as the womb of the world?
premises: What was described is called the cavity of maya.
Beyond it is the cave, which is the womb of the world.
Its generative activity occurs as the stirring of the lord and his power is followed among those beings.
items.inference: Beyond the cavity of maya lies the cave, a generative womb whose world-producing activity follows the stirring of the lord and his power.
uncertainties: The compound at the end is dense and its exact syntactic relations are somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: This has been called the cavity of maya. Beyond it is the cave, the womb of the world, whose arising takes place as the stirring of the lord and his power is followed among those beings.

items.question: What happens in the womb-openings called bhaga when the lord desires the goddess?
premises: There are womb-openings rich with various desires.
These openings are called bhaga.
When the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, that generative relation is activated.
items.inference: The bhaga-openings become the site of generative desire when the lord turns toward the goddess who accords with his will.
uncertainties: The verse is part of a larger sentence continued in the next verse.
items.plain_english: In the womb-openings, rich with various desires and called bhaga, when the lord desires the goddess who follows his will,

items.question: What is born in each bhaga when the lord desires the goddess, and how fully is it described?
premises: In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born.
These offspring are extremely subtle.
Their full extent is not described in the prescribed accounts.
items.inference: The generative union produces extremely subtle offspring in every bhaga, beginning with the unmanifest, beyond full scriptural description.
items.plain_english: then in each bhaga offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born from her. Because they are extremely subtle, their full extent is not described in the prescribed accounts.

items.question: How are the many womb-cavities within maya illustrated by analogy?
premises: Many inner rooms can be enclosed within one hall.
The womb-cavities are similarly enclosed within one head-hall of maya.
The verse uses a direct analogy to explain their arrangement.
items.inference: The multiplicity of womb-cavities exists within a single encompassing structure of maya, like rooms within one hall.
uncertainties: The term māyāśiraḥsāle is unusual and may be a technical cosmological expression.
items.plain_english: Just as many inner rooms are enclosed within one hall, so the womb-cavities are enclosed within the one head-hall of maya.

items.question: How do the Rudras dwell within the separate cavities of maya?
premises: The cavities are covered by subtle layers of maya like walls.
Because of these partitions, they are invisible to one another.
In each cavity innumerable happy Rudras dwell.
items.inference: Maya's subtle partitions create mutually hidden cavities, each inhabited by countless happy Rudras.
items.plain_english: Covered by subtle layers of maya like walls and invisible to one another, innumerable happy Rudras dwell there in each cavity.
